transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; what brings you in to see me today?

Hi Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you too. 

Well, what brought me in is that I've been realizing I keep getting up in meetings or at dinner when everyone else is seated. It's like... I'll suddenly feel the need to get up to refill my coffee, or go check a handout, or just walk to the back of the room. None of it is ever really urgent, but I just have a hard time staying in my chair when I'm supposed to.
When you feel the need to get up, is it because you are feeling overwhelmed by a sense of worry or nervous tension?

No, I wouldn't say that. It's not really a feeling of worry or... nervous tension. I don't feel anxious or overwhelmed at all when it happens. It's honestly just a physical urge to move around. My mind isn't racing with worries, I just get this feeling that I need to stand up and do something rather than just sit there.
Do you also find that you frequently make careless mistakes or struggle to pay close attention to details when you are working on tasks?

No, I wouldn't say so. I mean, as a secondary school teacher, I have to grade a lot of assignments and go over lesson plans, so I'm actually pretty used to paying attention to the details. I don't really find myself making careless mistakes with my work. It's really just the physical need to move around that I've been noticing.
Do you find that you have significant difficulty organizing your tasks or managing your time effectively in your daily life?

No, I don't think so. Um, my days are pretty structured at the school, so I don't really have trouble managing my time or keeping my tasks organized. I'm usually right on top of my schedule, actually.
Does this physical urge to move occur more often when you are trying to relax or lie down in the evening or at night?

No, I wouldn't say it's worse in the evening or at night. It's not really about lying down to sleep or relax at the end of the day. It just happens... well, anytime I have to sit still for a while, like if I'm stuck in a long staff meeting in the middle of the afternoon. So, no, I haven't noticed it being tied to nighttime.
Have you ever had significant problems with authority figures or found yourself frequently breaking rules or social norms throughout your life?

No, not at all. Um, being a teacher, I'm kind of on the other side of that. I've always been pretty much a rule-follower, so I've never really had any issues with authority figures or breaking rules. That's definitely not something I've ever struggled with.

When you feel that urge to stand up and move around, do you experience any uncomfortable or unpleasant sensations in your legs or arms, such as an itching, tingling, or pulling feeling, that is relieved by moving?

No, I don't feel anything like that. There's no itching or tingling or... anything uncomfortable in my legs or arms. It's really just a feeling of having too much energy, like I just need to get up and be doing something. But it's not because my body physically hurts or feels weird.
Looking back at your childhood, did you have this same persistent need to move around or difficulty staying seated in class when you were a student?

Yes, I did. Even as a young girl, my report cards always said that I was bright, but that I just could not stay in my seat or wait my turn. Um, my mother actually used to joke that I wore a path between my desk and the pencil sharpener before I was ten years old. So, yes, it's definitely been a lifelong thing.
Do you often find yourself blurting out answers before questions have been completed, or do you have a hard time waiting for your turn in conversations?

Yes, I do. Um, in group discussions, I often jump in before someone has finished their thought. I notice it a lot at my book club, or during curriculum meetings at school. The response is already right there in my head, and I just... I blurt it out before I can stop myself. It's definitely hard for me to wait my turn sometimes.

Do you find that you have significant difficulty sustaining your attention on tasks or activities, such as reading a long book or listening to an extended lecture, even if you are interested in the topic?

No, not really. I mean, if I'm interested in the book or the topic, I can usually focus on it just fine. It's more about sitting still while I'm doing it that's the problem. I don't really lose track of what I'm reading or listening to.
Do you often find yourself engaging in activities that are physically dangerous or risky without considering the potential consequences?

No, I wouldn't say that. I mean, I'm energetic and I like to keep moving, but I'm not reckless. I don't do things that are physically dangerous or put myself at risk like that. I've always been pretty sensible about safety, especially being a teacher.
